points.title: 童年启蒙
points.description: 玛格丽特·撒切尔出生于英格兰林肯郡的格兰瑟姆，父亲阿尔弗雷德·罗伯茨是当地杂货店主和卫理公会教堂的传道人。她的家庭中产阶级背景和严格的宗教信仰塑造了她早期的价值观。在格兰瑟姆女子文法学校学习期间，她展现出对化学和政治的浓厚兴趣，并担任学校辩论社主席。这段经历培养了她的雄辩能力和对政治的早期热情，为她日后进入政坛奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: Margaret Thatcher was born in Grantham, Lincolnshire, England, to Alfred Roberts, a local grocer and Methodist lay preacher. Her middle-class background and strict religious upbringing shaped her early values. At Grantham Girls' High School, she developed a keen interest in chemistry and politics, serving as president of the school's debating society. This experience cultivated her oratory skills and early passion for politics, laying the foundation for her future political career.

points.title: 牛津求学
points.description: 撒切尔进入牛津大学萨默维尔学院攻读化学专业，但她的兴趣逐渐转向政治。她积极参与保守党政治活动，担任牛津大学保守党协会主席，并成为该校历史上第一位女性主席。在此期间，她深受保守派思想家弗里德里希·哈耶克的影响，形成了坚定的自由市场经济理念。1947年，她以优异成绩获得化学学士学位，但决定投身政治而非科学研究，这一决定彻底改变了她的人生轨迹。
points.descriptionEn: Thatcher attended Somerville College, Oxford, to study chemistry, but her interests gradually shifted to politics. She actively participated in Conservative politics, becoming president of the Oxford University Conservative Association, the first woman to hold this position. During this time, she was deeply influenced by conservative thinker Friedrich Hayek, developing her strong belief in free-market economics. In 1947, she graduated with a chemistry degree but decided to pursue politics rather than scientific research, a decision that would fundamentally alter her life's trajectory.

points.title: 议会生涯
points.description: 1959年，撒切尔当选为芬奇利选区议员，正式进入英国下议院。在伦敦的议会生涯中，她逐步在保守党内崭露头角，先后担任影子内阁教育大臣、燃料和动力事务发言人等重要职务。1967年，她进入影子内阁，成为保守党前座议员中的核心人物。这一时期，她以强硬的辩论风格和对社会主义政策的批评而闻名，逐渐赢得了党内右翼的支持。1970年，保守党赢得大选后，爱德华·希思任命她为教育大臣，使她成为英国历史上第一位女性内阁大臣。
points.descriptionEn: In 1959, Thatcher was elected as the MP for Finchley, entering the British House of Commons. During her parliamentary career in London, she gradually rose within the Conservative Party, serving as Shadow Education Secretary, and later as spokesperson for fuel and power matters. By 1967, she had joined the Shadow Cabinet, becoming a central figure in the Conservative frontbench. During this period, she gained a reputation for her debating style and criticism of socialist policies, gradually winning support from the party's right wing. In 1970, after the Conservatives won the general election, Edward Heath appointed her as Secretary of State for Education and Science, making her the first woman to hold a cabinet position in British history.

points.title: 首相任期
points.description: 1979年，撒切尔成为英国历史上第一位女性首相，开始了长达11年的执政。在唐宁街10号期间，她推行了一系列激进的经济改革政策，包括私有化国有企业、削减福利支出、限制工会权力等，这些政策后来被称为'撒切尔主义'。她坚定支持英国参与欧洲共同体，但在主权问题上持强硬立场。1982年，她领导英国赢得马岛战争，极大地提升了她的政治威望。1984-1985年的矿工工潮是她与工会力量的直接对抗。1980年代末，她推动英国与美国密切合作，在冷战末期发挥了重要作用。1990年，由于党内分歧和政策争议，她被迫辞去首相职务。
points.descriptionEn: In 1979, Thatcher became the first female Prime Minister in British history, beginning an 11-year tenure at 10 Downing Street. During this period, she implemented a series of radical economic reforms, including privatizing state-owned enterprises, cutting welfare spending, and restricting union power—policies later known as 'Thatcherism.' She strongly supported Britain's participation in the European Community but took a hard line on sovereignty issues. In 1982, she led Britain to victory in the Falklands War, significantly boosting her political standing. The 1984-1985 miners' strike represented a direct confrontation with union power. By the late 1980s, she fostered close cooperation with the United States, playing an important role during the final stages of the Cold War. In 1990, she resigned as Prime Minister due to internal party divisions and policy controversies.

points.title: 退休生活
points.description: 离开唐宁街后，撒切尔继续活跃于政治舞台，撰写回忆录并发表演讲。1992年，她被封为终身贵族，进入上议院。她继续保持对政治的关注，特别是对欧洲一体化持批评态度，反对英国加入欧元区。1990年代中期，她健康状况开始恶化，记忆力衰退，但仍然偶尔发表评论。2002年，在丈夫丹尼斯去世后，她的公开活动大幅减少。2003年，她因中风去世，享年87岁。她的葬礼是英国近半个世纪以来规模最大的国葬之一，反映了她在英国历史上的重要地位。
points.descriptionEn: After leaving Downing Street, Thatcher remained active in politics, writing memoirs and giving speeches. In 1992, she was elevated to the House of Lords as a life peer. She continued to follow political developments closely, particularly criticizing European integration and opposing British adoption of the euro. In the mid-1990s, her health began to decline with memory problems, though she occasionally made public statements. After her husband Denis's death in 2003, her public appearances significantly decreased. She suffered a stroke and died in 2003 at the age of 87. Her funeral was one of the largest state funerals in Britain in nearly half a century, reflecting her significant place in British history.

points.title: 历史遗产
points.description: 撒切尔去世后，她的政治遗产继续在英国乃至全球范围内引发讨论。她被支持者誉为'铁娘子'，认为她重塑了英国经济，恢复了国家自信。她的政策影响了全球保守主义运动，被称为'撒切尔革命'。然而，批评者认为她的政策加剧了社会不平等，摧毁了传统工业基础。2013年，电影《铁娘子》上映，进一步将她塑造为具有争议性的历史人物。2016年英国脱欧公投后，她的名字再次成为政治辩论的焦点，被视为英国主权和独立精神的象征。她的政治理念和政策影响持续影响着英国政治格局。
points.descriptionEn: After Thatcher's death, her political legacy continued to spark debate in Britain and globally. Admired by supporters as the 'Iron Lady,' she is credited with reshaping the British economy and restoring national confidence. Her policies influenced global conservatism, known as the 'Thatcher Revolution.' However, critics argue that her policies exacerbated social inequality and destroyed traditional industrial bases. In 2013, the film 'The Iron Lady' was released, further cementing her status as a controversial historical figure. Following the 2016 Brexit referendum, her name once again became central to political debate, symbolizing British sovereignty and independence. Her political philosophy and policies continue to influence the British political landscape.

supporter.zh: 撒切尔被支持者誉为英国战后最伟大的首相之一，她通过坚定的政治意志和大胆的经济改革，将英国从'病夫'状态转变为经济活力充沛的国家。她推行私有化政策提高了效率，削减福利支出控制了财政赤字，限制工会权力恢复了经济秩序。在马岛战争中展现的领导力重振了英国的国际地位。她打破了政治性别天花板，成为女性领导力的象征，激励了全球无数女性进入政治领域。撒切尔主义重塑了英国政治经济格局，其影响延续至今。
supporter.en: Thatcher is regarded by supporters as one of Britain's greatest post-war prime ministers. Through unwavering political will and bold economic reforms, she transformed Britain from a 'sick man' of Europe into an economically vibrant nation. Her privatization policies increased efficiency, welfare cuts controlled budget deficits, and restricting union power restored economic order. Her leadership during the Falklands War revitalized Britain's international standing. She broke the political gender ceiling, becoming a symbol of female leadership that inspired countless women worldwide to enter politics. Thatcherism reshaped Britain's political and economic landscape, with effects that continue to this day.

critic.zh: 批评者认为撒切尔的政策造成了严重的社会分裂和经济不平等。大规模私有化导致国有资产流失，公共服务质量下降，失业率飙升。她削减社会福利的政策使弱势群体生活更加艰难，社区凝聚力被破坏。与工会的强硬对抗加剧了劳资矛盾，北方工业地区遭受重创，形成了所谓的'南北差距'。她的外交政策过于亲美，损害了英国在欧洲的地位。批评者指责她缺乏社会关怀，只关注经济增长而忽视了社会公正，认为她的遗产是分裂而非团结。
critic.en: Critics argue that Thatcher's policies created severe social division and economic inequality. Mass privatization led to the loss of public assets, declining quality of public services, and soaring unemployment. Her welfare cuts made life more difficult for vulnerable groups, weakening community cohesion. Her confrontational approach to unions exacerbated labor conflicts, devastating industrial regions in the north and creating what became known as the 'North-South divide.' Her foreign policy was overly pro-American, damaging Britain's position in Europe. Critics accuse her of lacking social concern, focusing solely on economic growth while neglecting social justice, arguing her legacy is division rather than unity.

objective.zh: 历史学界普遍认为撒切尔是20世纪最具影响力的政治家之一，她的政策重塑了英国政治经济格局。在冷战背景下，她坚定支持美国，推动了西方阵营的团结。她打破了英国政治中的性别障碍，为女性参政开辟了道路。她的经济政策虽争议巨大，但确实提高了英国经济的效率和竞争力。在流行文化中，'铁娘子'成为强硬女性领导者的代名词，她的形象被不断重塑和解读。撒切尔主义作为一种政治理念，影响了全球保守主义运动，其遗产至今仍在英国政治辩论中占据重要位置。
objective.en: Historians widely regard Thatcher as one of the most influential politicians of the 20th century, whose policies reshaped Britain's political and economic landscape. Against the backdrop of the Cold War, she staunchly supported the United States, strengthening Western unity. She broke gender barriers in British politics, paving the way for women's political participation. Her economic policies, though highly controversial, did improve the efficiency and competitiveness of the British economy. In popular culture, 'Iron Lady' has become synonymous with strong female leadership, with her image continuously reinterpreted. Thatcherism as a political philosophy influenced global conservatism, and its legacy remains central to British political debates today.

self.zh: 我不是一个寻求共识的政治家，我是一个有信念的政治家。
self.en: I am not a consensus politician. I am a conviction politician.

others.zh: 玛格丽特·撒切尔是20世纪最具变革性的政治家之一，她改变了英国的政治和经济方向，其影响将持续数十年。
others.en: Margaret Thatcher was one of the most transformative politicians of the 20th century; she changed the direction of British politics and economics, and her influence will be felt for decades to come.
